title: One Purchase, Start to Finish
tagline: Follow a single order from empty bin to paid invoice — and catch what goes wrong on the way.

cast.storyRole: approves, picks the vendor, sends the PO

seo.description: Learn the procure-to-pay cycle by running one real purchase end to end: requisition, approval, vendor choice, PO, receiving, and the 3-way match.

glossary.definition: An internal raised hand: a request for approval to buy. Marcus raised one when the titanium dioxide bin ran low — it never goes to any vendor.
The binding document sent to the vendor: what, how much, at what price, by when. Once acknowledged, both sides are committed.
Comparing PO, goods receipt, and invoice before paying. If the three don't agree, somebody is about to pay for something that didn't happen.

lines.text: The titanium dioxide bin is down to eight days of stock, and Crestline needs six to deliver. If we sit on this, we'll be counting hours instead of days.
I'm raising a requisition now — Diana needs to see this before lunch, not before Friday.

payload.prompt: Line 2 uses about 650 kg a day. The usual vendor delivers in 6 days. How much should Diana approve?

choices.label: 2,000 kg
choices.implication: About 3 days of cover after arrival
choices.feedback: That covers the gap only if nothing slips. One late truck and Line 2 stops anyway.

choices.label: 4,500 kg
choices.implication: About 7 days of cover after arrival
choices.feedback: Covers the 6-day lead time plus a buffer for a late delivery, without freezing a month of cash in powder.

choices.label: 9,000 kg
choices.implication: Two weeks of cover — and a full warehouse rack
choices.feedback: Safe, but that's cash sitting on a shelf and rack space you don't have. Over-ordering is a cost too, just a quieter one.

payload.teachingPoint: Order quantity is a cash-versus-risk decision: cover the lead time plus realistic slippage, not your anxiety.

payload.prompt: Three vendors can supply. Titanium dioxide is a critical raw material. Who gets the order?

options.name: PrimeChem Direct
options.note: No quality audit on file for a critical material.

payload.feedbackCorrect: Right. On a critical material, a proven vendor at $1.85 beats an unaudited one at $1.62 — the 23-cent saving is smaller than the cost of one stopped line.
payload.feedbackWrong: Tempting price — but an unverified vendor on a critical material is how production lines stop. The saving doesn't survive one bad batch.
payload.teachingPoint: Vendor selection prices in risk, not just dollars per kg. Critical materials earn stricter rules.

payload.intro: Diana drafted the PO in a hurry. Check it before it goes out.

fields.label: Unit of Measure
fields.explanation: Titanium dioxide is a powder bought by weight. A vendor shipping 4,500 liters would deliver the wrong quantity entirely.

fields.label: Delivery Address
fields.explanation: Bay 5 is finished goods. Raw material trucks that arrive there get turned away — and the clock restarts.

payload.teachingPoint: A PO error becomes everyone's error downstream — receiving, accounts, and the vendor all inherit it.

payload.prompt: The truck arrives and 4,500 kg checks in clean. Leon starts the match: what should Crestline's invoice line total be?
payload.teachingPoint: The 3-way match starts with arithmetic anyone can do — and catches errors nobody else will.

questions.prompt: Crestline's invoice arrives showing 4,700 kg. The GRN says 4,500 kg. What does Leon do?

options.text: Pay it — the difference is small
Hold payment and query the mismatch with the vendor
Edit the GRN to 4,700 so the documents agree

questions.explanation: The match failed, so payment stops until the documents agree. Editing the GRN to force agreement is how companies pay for goods that never arrived.

questions.prompt: Which document committed Nexara to the price?
questions.explanation: The PR asks internally; the GRN records arrival. The PO is the binding commercial document both sides committed to.

takeaways: Procure-to-pay is one chain: PR → Approval → Vendor → PO → GRN → Invoice match → Payment.
Every document exists to catch a specific kind of error before it becomes money.
Vendor choice on critical materials is a risk decision, not a price decision.
When the 3-way match fails, payment stops — the documents are made to agree by investigation, never by editing.
